Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology degree program, prospective students must have a bachelor’s degree in Anthropology or a related field (e.g., Sociology, Geography, History, Political Science, Philosophy, Religious Studies, Women’s and Gender Studies, Environmental Studies). Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in a non-related field may be considered for admission if their undergraduate training or professional experience has provided appropriate background. Students who are admitted but lack sufficient background in anthropology may be required to complete preparatory coursework. Application to the MA in Applied Anthropology program is a two-part process requiring applicants to apply to both the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Anthropology. You must provide the following materials to the Toulouse Graduate School: An official transcript from each college or university you have attended. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing). You must provide the following materials to the Department of Anthropology: A current curriculum vita (CV) or resume. A Statement of Purpose that explains your academic and research background, your interest in the MA in Applied Anthropology program at UNT, and your career goals, as well as an identification of one or more faculty members with whom you would like to work and why (approximately 1,000 words). A writing sample (e.g., a paper or thesis from an undergraduate course). Three letters of recommendation. For international applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), IELTS score of 6.0, or PTE score of 53 is required. The departmental recommendation is a minimum TOEFL score of 90 (internet-based).
Program name: Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology

Requirements:
In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Art Education must meet the following program requirements:
* A strong interest in art education.
* Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in undergraduate work.
* Resume or CV
* Statement of purpose explaining your interest in art education and professional goals.
* Two letters of recommendation, with at least one from a university faculty member.
* Writing sample of an academic paper completed during undergraduate or previous graduate work (5-10 pages).
* Portfolio of 10-15 images of recent artwork. Include a list of images (title, medium, dimensions, date). Applicants will upload their writing sample and portfolio to their personal Slideroom account, accessed through the application.
* Official GRE scores are not required for admission.
* International applicants must fulfill requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School regarding English proficiency.
Program name: Master of Arts in Art Education

Requirements:
In addition to the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants to the MA in Art History must meet the following departmental requirements:
1. An undergraduate major in art history or 18 semester hours of advanced courses in art history that are approved by the department.
2. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0.
3. Three letters of recommendation submitted directly to the Graduate School.
4. A statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum) outlining the student’s interests in art history and reasons for pursuing graduate study.
5. A writing sample (8-10 pages) that demonstrates the student’s ability to write critically and clearly about art history. This should be an essay written for an advanced undergraduate art history course.
6. A CV or resume.
7. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
8. GRE scores are NOT required for admission to the MA program in Art History.
Program name: Master of Arts in Art History

Requirements: Admission to the M.A. program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better and a combined Verbal and Quantitative score of 300 or better on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE). The analytical writing score from the GRE is also taken into consideration. To apply for the M.A. in Communication Studies, you must submit the following: A completed application for graduate admission. Official transcripts of all college-level work. Official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing). A statement of purpose (1,000 words max) that explains your interest in the MA program in Communication Studies at UNT, your research interests, and your professional goals. A current resume or CV. A writing sample (e.g., a scholarly paper, a research paper, a chapter from an undergraduate thesis, etc.) that demonstrates your ability to write clearly and persuasively. For additional information, see the Communication Studies Graduate Catalog.
Program name: Master of Arts in Communication Studies

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MA in Creative Writing, applicants must meet the following requirements in addition to the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 grade point average on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Statement of Purpose that explains the applicant's reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in Creative Writing, outlining previous experience in the field and discussing literary influences. Resume (or curriculum vitae) listing academic and professional achievements. Writing Sample of 15-25 pages of original fiction, poetry or creative nonfiction. Applicants must identify the genre of the writing sample. Three letters of recommendation from former professors or professionals who can attest to the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional aptitudes.
Program name: Master of Arts in Creative Writing

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MA in English program, an applicant must satisfy the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, hold a bachelor’s degree with an undergraduate major in English, or at least 18 hours of upper-division English credit, including a minimum of three hours in American literature, three hours in British literature, and three hours in advanced writing. Applicants are also required to submit a personal statement (300-500 words) and a critical writing sample (8-10 pages) demonstrating their ability to formulate and support an argument about literary texts. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation from faculty members familiar with their academic work.
Program name: Master of Arts in English

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and the following program requirements: One official transcript of all college work. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and/or a 3.5 GPA on all graduate work. GRE revised General Test required. A minimum score of 153 on the verbal portion, 144 on the quantitative portion, and 4.0 on the analytical writing portion is recommended. A statement of purpose (1,000 words, double-spaced) describing your previous academic and/or professional training, the areas of history you propose to study at UNT, and your future career goals. A writing sample (8-15 pages, double-spaced) demonstrating your ability to conduct research and write a scholarly paper. Three letters of recommendation from former professors who are familiar with your academic work. Resume/CV (optional).
Program name: Master of Arts in History

Requirements: A formal application to The Graduate School and the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to The Graduate School. GRE is required.
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies

Requirements: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) general test is required. Statement of Purpose. Two letters of recommendation. Resume.
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Applied Gerontology

Requirements: Completion of a bachelor's degree. A strong academic record, typically a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional experience. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that addresses: Why you are interested in the MAIS program and the Digital Social Science concentration specifically; How your academic and professional background has prepared you for this interdisciplinary program; Your research interests and career goals, and how this program aligns with them. A curriculum vitae or resume. GRE scores are NOT required.
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Digital Social Science

Requirements: Admission to the master’s program is open to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, which are listed in the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog. In addition to meeting the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities must submit: An essay (2-5 pages) explaining how the applicant's prior academic and/or professional experiences have prepared them for interdisciplinary study in the humanities and what they hope to achieve through the program. This essay serves as a writing sample and statement of purpose. Three letters of recommendation, at least two from university faculty familiar with the applicant’s academic performance. Official transcripts of all college-level work. An academic resume or curriculum vitae (CV) describing previous education, employment history and any other information relevant to graduate study. GRE Scores: Applicants whose undergraduate GPA is less than 3.0 must also submit official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Applicants who are required to take the GRE must also include an unofficial copy of their scores in their application packet.
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities

Requirements: You must meet the general requirements for admission to the graduate school and specific requirements for the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication. General Admission Requirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. (You may also be admitted if you demonstrate equivalent academic achievement.) An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (or a minimum score on the GRE). Satisfactory performance on the GRE General Test, if required by the program. Degree-specific Admission Requirements: For the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication, you must also: Possess a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA on 12 hours of graduate coursework (or a GRE total score of 292 with a minimum of 146 on both the verbal and quantitative sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing section).
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication

Requirements:
Admission to the Interdisciplinary Studies, M.A. program requires the following:
*   GRE general test scores. Official GRE scores are required for all applicants.
*   Statement of purpose. Required.
*   Writing sample. Required.
*   Three letters of recommendation. Required.
*   Resume or curriculum vitae. Required.
*   Application to the Toulouse Graduate School. All prospective graduate students must apply for admission to UNT’s Toulouse Graduate School.
Program name: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Program Leadership

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the M.A. program in International Studies, applicants should apply online through the Toulouse Graduate School and submit the following documents directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Transcripts must be sent directly from the institution in a sealed envelope or through a secure electronic method to the Toulouse Graduate School. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability and potential for success in graduate school. Letters of recommendation should be submitted directly by the recommenders to the Toulouse Graduate School. Statement of Purpose: A two-page (double-spaced) statement outlining your academic and professional goals, research interests, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in International Studies at UNT. The statement should demonstrate your writing ability and analytical skills. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV): A current resume or CV highlighting your educational background, work experience, research projects, publications, presentations, and any other relevant experience. Writing Sample: An academic paper, essay, or research project (8-15 pages in length) that demonstrates your research, analytical, and writing skills. The writing sample should preferably be on a topic related to international studies or political science. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores are NOT required for admission to the MA in International Studies program. For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency is required (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test scores). Please refer to the Toulouse Graduate School website for specific requirements.
Program name: Master of Arts in International Studies

Requirements: Review the University requirements for graduate admission. Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores. If required by the department, official GRE scores must be sent directly from the Educational Testing Service (ETS) to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School (code 6480). For more information, visit the GRE General Test website. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International students may be required to submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. 3.0 GPA minimum in the last 60 undergraduate hours. Writing sample – maximum 10 pages. Please choose work that reflects your best writing ability, whether academic or professional. If you do not have any writing that you feel showcases your best work, consider writing a new piece specifically for this application. Resume (Required). Statement of Purpose (Required). Three (3) letters of recommendation.
Program name: Master of Arts in Journalism

Requirements: Admission to the master’s program in Media Industry and Critical Studies is contingent on admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and on the recommendation of the department. The decision to admit a student to the program is based on a holistic review of all application materials and considers factors related to the applicant’s background and aptitude for graduate study in media studies. Applicants must satisfy the following additional requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are not required to have an undergraduate degree in media studies or a related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that describes the applicant’s academic interests and goals, relevant experiences, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in Media Industry and Critical Studies at UNT. A writing sample (e.g., an academic paper, professional report, or published article) that demonstrates the applicant’s analytical and writing abilities. Official GRE scores are not required. A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).
Program name: Master of Arts in Media Industry and Critical Studies
Master of Arts in Music

The following items are required for your application: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation addressing your academic abilities. A statement of purpose outlining your philosophical interests and your reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in philosophy at UNT. A writing sample of 10-20 pages (preferably philosophical).
Program name: Master of Arts in Philosophy

Requirements: Applicants must meet the following general requirements to be considered for admission to the M.A. program in political science. Meeting these requirements does not guarantee admission. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale over the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework (or 3.0 overall for students with less than 60 hours of undergraduate coursework). A strong letter of intent (statement of purpose). Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional potential. A writing sample of no more than 20 pages. A background in political science, history, economics, or another relevant discipline. Minimum scores on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test are required for students with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0. For students with an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher, the GRE is optional. International applicants must also meet UNT's English Language Proficiency requirements.
Program name: Master of Arts in Political Science

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts program in political science is open to students holding a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the following requirements for unconditional admission:
1. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate hours.
2. A combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE).
3. Two letters of recommendation from former instructors who can attest to the applicant’s academic preparedness and scholarly potential. Applicants with a period of professional work experience may substitute one letter from a professional supervisor.
4. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-700 words) describing the applicant’s academic interests and career goals. The statement should also address how the applicant’s academic and/or professional background has prepared them for graduate study in political science at UNT.
5. A writing sample demonstrating the applicant’s ability to conduct research and write an analytical essay. Typically, this is a research paper prepared for a previous political science course. No minimum or maximum length is specified, but the applicant should choose a sample that best demonstrates their writing and analytical skills.
Program name: Master of Arts in Political Science with a concentration in Advocacy, Politics and Policy

Requirements: Admission to the Graduate School requires a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution and a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission. Additional requirements for the Professional and Technical Communication MA program include: A two-page, single-spaced statement of purpose addressing your academic and professional experience and how the Professional and Technical Communication program will help you meet your career goals; An updated résumé or curriculum vitae; An academic or professional writing sample of approximately 10-20 pages; Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; The GRE is not required for admission to the MA program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Professional and Technical Communication

Requirements: An applicant must meet the university requirements for admission to graduate school as well as the following departmental requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework. A minimum of 24 upper-level undergraduate hours in Spanish, including courses in composition, culture, civilization, literature and linguistics, with a minimum grade of B in all Spanish courses. An academic writing sample, preferably in Spanish. A statement of purpose, preferably in Spanish, describing their interest in graduate study in Spanish at UNT. A letter of recommendation (optional). Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test, with a minimum of 145 (quantitative) and 153 (verbal) on the revised test (or equivalent on the previous test); or a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework.
Program name: Master of Arts in Spanish

A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are not required to have an undergraduate major in women's and gender studies, but must demonstrate previous coursework or experience in the field.
An undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
GRE scores are not required for admission to the MA in Women's and Gender Studies.
Three letters of recommendation addressing academic qualifications and scholarly potential.

- Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Program name: Master of Arts in Women's and Gender Studies

Every part of your application provides valuable insights into your qualifications, and we encourage you to spend time preparing each component. To complete the application, you will need to provide: Academic Transcripts, GMAT/GRE/Executive Assessment (EA) Test Scores, English Language Proficiency (if applicable), Essays, Resume, Recommendation, Application Fee.
Program name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)

Program name: Master of Business Administration in Business Analytics
Master of Business Administration in Management Consulting

For consideration for admission into the MBA Program, prospective students must submit an application and the following supporting documents:
*   Official transcripts for all coursework
*   GMAT or GRE (test waiver option available)
*   Resume or Vita (CV): Required
*   Statement of Purpose (essay): Required
*   Three letters of recommendation

*   Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   Have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in previous graduate coursework.
*   Submit scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE), taken within the last five years.
*   Submit a two-page, double-spaced essay discussing career goals and professional experiences.
*   Submit three letters of recommendation with at least two from a faculty member and one from a supervisor in a professional setting.

Master of Education in Curriculum and Instruction

Requirements: The following materials should be submitted as part of your online application: Official Transcripts; GRE test scores (optional based on GPA); Upload a current resume or vita.; Upload a personal statement describing career goals, relevant experience, and reasons for pursuing a master’s degree in educational leadership.; A copy of your valid teaching certificate.; Letter of recommendation from your current supervisor or principal.
Program name: Master of Education in Educational Leadership

Requirements: All applicants must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to the Graduate School requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants may be admitted to the program provisionally or conditionally while completing remaining undergraduate coursework, not to exceed 12 hours. Provisional/conditional admission requires a minimum GPA of 2.8 and approval of the program coordinator. Full admission requires a minimum GPA of 3.0. Three letters of recommendation are required from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic and/or professional potential. Letters of recommendation must be submitted through the ApplyTexas online application system. Admission to the program is competitive. Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
Program name: Master of Education in Higher Education

Requirements: In addition to the Graduate School admission requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Hold a bachelor’s degree. Have a minimum 2.8 undergraduate GPA or a 3.0 GPA on the last 60 undergraduate hours. If GPA is less than 2.8, must submit GRE scores. Have a valid Texas Teacher Certification in Special Education EC-12 (preferred but not required). Submit a professional resume/CV. Submit an essay (statement of purpose) clearly articulating your purpose for pursuing a master’s degree in special education, including the relationship to your professional goals. Submit a signed copy of the Department of Educational Psychology’s Disclaimer Form. Provide three (3) letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of your academic ability and/or professional experience. Have a minimum of two years of teaching experience (preferred but not required). Interview with faculty.
Program name: Master of Education in Special Education

Requirements: Students seeking admission to the Master of Education in Teaching must have: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential or professional experience. A personal statement (500 words maximum) indicating the applicant's reasons for pursuing graduate study in education. Current resume/curriculum vitae (CV) detailing educational background, work experience, volunteer activities, and any relevant achievements. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For international students, TOEFL/IELTS scores as required by the university.
Program name: Master of Education in Teaching

Requirements:
All applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to those requirements, applicants to the M.A. or M.F.A. in Design must meet the following program requirements:
*   A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and a 3.0 GPA on any previous graduate work.
*   Submission of the following directly to the CVAD Graduate Office (cvadgrad@unt.edu):
    *   Statement of Purpose
    *   Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume

Master of Fine Arts in Design with a concentration in Interior Design

Transcripts must be sent directly to UNT from the issuing institution. The GRE is not required for admission. Submit three (3) letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability and potential for success in a graduate program. Submit a statement of purpose (2-3 pages, double-spaced) that addresses the following: why you are interested in the program, how you expect to benefit from it, what you believe you will contribute to the field, and your career goals. Requirements: You must submit a non-refundable application fee. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic and professional accomplishments are required. These are submitted directly by your recommenders through the online application portal. A statement of purpose outlining your goals, interests and reasons for pursuing an MFA in Studio Art is required. You must provide official transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended. A CV or Resume is required for your application to the MFA in Studio Art program. An artist statement (500 words maximum) is required describing your current artistic practice and interests. A portfolio is required and submitted through Slideroom.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Studio Art

Requirements:
1. Graduate School application with application fee.
2. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
3. GRE scores. See Jazz Studies website for exceptions/waivers.
4. For additional admission requirements, see the Jazz Studies website.
Program name: Master of Music in Jazz Studies

Requirements: Students applying to any of the graduate programs in the College of Music must have an undergraduate degree in music or its equivalent. Students must be fully admitted to The Graduate School AND the College of Music to pursue a graduate degree in music. Official transcripts must be submitted from all universities and colleges previously attended, including a bachelor’s degree in music. Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency. Two letters of recommendation from individuals able to assess your academic potential are required. An audition is required for all MM, DMA, and Performer’s Certificate applicants in Performance, including concentrations in Jazz Performance and Instrumental/Vocal Performance; contact the area for specifics.
Program name: Master of Music in Performance

Requirements: All graduate students applying to the University of North Texas College of Music must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School AND complete a College of Music Application. Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an institution accredited by a recognized U.S. accrediting agency or an equivalent international institution, with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (or the last 2 years) and in any previous graduate work. Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities are required. Three (3) letters of recommendation are required for all graduate applicants. For the Master of Music Education program, applicants must have completed an undergraduate degree in music education, or a bachelor’s degree in music with at least 15 semester hours of professional music education coursework and one year of successful teaching experience.
Program name: Master of Music Education

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. These include: a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution, official transcripts from all institutions attended, and an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. Additionally, three letters of recommendation are required. International Applicants must meet additional requirements specific to international applicants, including English language proficiency as evidenced by an official TOEFL score of 79 on the internet-based test or an official IELTS score of 6.0 overall. The deadline for applications to the MPA program is February 1st for fall admissions and October 1st for spring admissions.
Program name: Master of Public Administration (MPA)

Official GRE or GMAT scores (optional, but encouraged). Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. International students may be required to submit a TOEFL or IELTS score. Departmental Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in accounting or an equivalent degree. Completion of undergraduate course work comparable to UNT's BBA in Accounting requirements with a grade of "B" or better. Satisfactory performance on the CPA exam's business environment and concepts section may substitute for certain prerequisite courses.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting with a concentration in Audit and Data Analytics

Requirements: All applicants must meet the UNT Texas Graduate School admission requirements. Students seeking admission to the M.S. in Accounting program must submit the following materials directly to the Department of Accounting for review: Official GMAT scores (Minimum GMAT score of 500 required for full admission; Minimum GMAT score of 450 required for conditional admission), official academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, undergraduate grade point average (GPA) (Minimum 3.0 GPA for full admission; Minimum 2.8 GPA for conditional admission), a personal statement that describes your background, interests and goals regarding graduate study in accounting at UNT, as well as your career aspirations, a current resume, and two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic and professional accomplishments.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting with a concentration in Corporate Accounting

Requirements: You must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 undergraduate semester hours and in any previous graduate work. GRE is NOT REQUIRED. Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable about the applicant’s academic preparation and ability to succeed in graduate school. A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic objectives, professional goals, and reasons for pursuing the program. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Program name: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science degree program in Advanced Data Analytics is contingent on admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and satisfaction of the following requirements:
*   Baccalaureate degree: An undergraduate degree in a related field from an accredited institution (e.g., business, computer science, economics, engineering, mathematics, statistics).
*   GPA: A minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a 3.0 GPA on previous graduate work.
*   Prerequisites: Completion of undergraduate courses in programming (e.g., Python, R, Java, C++, SAS, SQL), linear algebra, and statistics with a grade of B or better, or completion of equivalent graduate courses. Students without these prerequisites will be required to take them.
*   English Language Proficiency: International applicants must satisfy the UNT International Admissions English Language Proficiency requirements.
Additional materials required for all applicants:
1.  Resume: A current resume highlighting education, work experience, research, volunteer activities, and any relevant data analytics skills or projects.
2.  Statement of Purpose: A 750-1000 word statement explaining your interest in the Advanced Data Analytics program, your career goals, and how your academic and professional experiences have prepared you for success in the program.
3.  Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can assess your academic and/or professional capabilities and potential for success in a graduate program.
4.  Official Transcripts: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.

If an applicant has less than a 3.0 GPA, they may be admitted provisionally if they have a minimum 2.8 GPA on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours and an acceptable GRE score. Admission to the PSM program requires a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry or a related field. Students should have completed a year of general chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry and physical chemistry. The department may require a student to take additional courses as prerequisites if they do not have sufficient background.
Program name: Master of Science in Professional Science Master's degree option (chemistry)

Requirements: UNT's College of Health and Public Service and Toulouse Graduate School require applicants to meet the following criteria: A bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution, undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher, and GRE and/or other admission exams are not required. Specific application requirements for this program are listed below: Submit all official transcripts, a personal statement/statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum) indicating your interest in rehabilitation counseling as a profession and your professional goals, three letters of recommendation addressing your potential for success in a graduate program, your professional experience, and your ability to work with diverse populations, a resume or vita that demonstrates work and volunteer experience in human service, rehabilitation, or related fields, and successful completion of an interview with program faculty.
Program name: Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling

Requirements: Candidates for the MS in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering must meet the following requirements to be admitted to the program: Official GRE scores, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose, Official transcripts, Undergraduate GPA, Minimum GRE scores (146 Verbal, 146 Quantitative, 3.5 Analytical Writing). Applicants for the Master of Science in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering must apply to The Graduate School and meet the following requirements specific to the program: Admission to the Master of Science program requires: A bachelor’s degree in engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 overall and 3.0 in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose (500-1000 words). Official GRE scores: minimum of 146 Verbal, 146 Quantitative, and 3.5 Analytical Writing. Applicants who have earned a master’s degree from an accredited institution in an engineering or closely related field are exempt from the GRE requirement.
Program name: Master of Science in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering

Requirements:
Admission to the MSW program is limited to applicants who show promise for successful graduate study and and professional social work practice. The admissions committee reviews all applications submitted to the program. An applicant must submit an application packet directly to the Department of Social Work as well as an application to the Toulouse Graduate School (TGS).
TGS Application Packet Requirements:
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended.
A Statement of Purpose (no more than three double-spaced pages describing your interest in social work, experience, and professional goals).
Resume/vita outlining academic background, paid and volunteer work experience, and any professional or community service.
Three letters of recommendation (at least two should be academic or professional; letters from friends/family will not be accepted).
GRE General Test scores if undergraduate GPA is below 3.0.
Department Application Packet Requirements:
A Social Work Addendum Application (available at socialwork.unt.edu).
A writing sample is not required for admission.
Program name: Master of Science in Social Work (MSW)

Requirements:
Applicants for the M.S. and Ph.D. programs should apply through the Toulouse Graduate School. Application details and deadlines are available at the Toulouse Graduate School Application webpage. Additional materials, such as those listed below, should be submitted electronically through the Toulouse Graduate School’s online application system.

Official Transcripts: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Applicants must have completed a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.

Three Letters of Recommendation: Sent from academic faculty members or others who can evaluate the applicant’s potential for success in graduate school.

International Student Applicants: All international applicants must meet the UNT international admission requirements found on the Toulouse Graduate School website. Additionally, international students must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores according to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School Requirements.
Program name: Master of Science in Sociology

Requirements: In addition to the requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the department: Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test, taken within the last five years. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing interest in the field of speech-language pathology, professional goals, and relevant experiences. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential, work ethic, and ability to complete graduate-level work. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Completion of specific prerequisite coursework in communication sciences and disorders or related fields. Details can be found on the department website.
Program name: Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology
Master of Science in Taxation and Data Analytics

Requirements: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Applicants must submit a separate application to the UNT Health Science Center via the Communication Sciences and Disorders Centralized Application Service (CSDCAS) at www.csdcas.org. A minimum of 25 observation hours in audiology is required. A minimum of 3 letters of recommendation is required. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required. TOEFL/IELTS: If English is not the applicant's native language, the applicant must demonstrate English proficiency as specified by the UNT Health Science Center.
Program name: Doctor of Audiology (AuD)

Requirements: Admission to the DBA program is based on a review of the entire application file. Strong applicants will have relevant work experience, excellent academic records, leadership potential, and outstanding critical thinking and communication skills. In addition to the Graduate School requirements, applicants must provide: Online Application and Application Fee, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, Official GMAT or GRE scores are required, with the exception of waivers. Please note the UNT Graduate School requires official scores. Personal Statement, Resume/CV, Three letters of recommendation, For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency.
Program name: Doctor of Business Administration (DBA)

Requirements: The DMA program is designed for the highly talented musician who has demonstrated exceptional promise through previous academic degrees and performance. It is a three-year residency degree that combines comprehensive coursework and intensive instruction for the highest artistic and academic achievement. Areas of study include Music History, Music Theory, and other music-related courses. Students seeking the DMA degree must audition for entrance, in addition to meeting the standard UNT TGS and College of Music requirements. All graduate applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s general admission requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution; Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours or a 3.0 on all undergraduate work; Official transcripts from all universities attended; Official scores for English Language Proficiency (ELP), if required (International applicants); Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores, if required by your program of interest. Graduate students wishing to apply to any degree program in the College of Music must complete two applications: the UNT Toulouse Graduate School application and the College of Music graduate application. In addition to the online application, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the College of Music (via the online application form): Curriculum Vitae/Resume – an overview of your academic and performance/professional experience; Statement of Purpose – a statement of your academic and professional goals, including a discussion of your interest in the UNT College of Music. (Maximum of 500 words). DMA applicants must also submit (in addition to the above): Repertoire List – a representative list of your previous performance repertoire; Writing Sample (DMA Performance only) – a paper written on a musical topic (e.g., from a music history/theory course); Interview/Audition.
Program name: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Performance

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Minimum GPA of 3.0 in Master’s degree coursework. Official GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. Required Application Materials: Toulouse Graduate School application, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of intent, Professional vita or resume, Writing sample (a research paper, critical essay, or similar academic text), Portfolio of creative works (or a statement about why a portfolio is not included and alternative documentation), Interview (by invitation, after review of application), International students must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores (unless exempted).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and the following program requirements: Minimum 3.0 GPA in previous work. GRE scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) submitted directly from ETS. GRE scores must be less than 5 years old. There is no minimum score requirement; however, competitive applicants typically score above the 50th percentile on the verbal and quantitative sections. Three letters of recommendation. Required Documents: Curriculum Vitae or Resume, Statement of Purpose, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For information about the application and admission process, including admission to the Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and for international students, visit the UNT Graduate Admissions website.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Behavioral Science

Requirements: Minimum GPA: 3.0, Official GRE scores, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose (required for both PhD and MS applicants), Current resume or curriculum vitae, Supplemental Application Form (Required by department)
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Robert B. Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and must also meet specific program requirements. All application materials must be submitted through the Toulouse Graduate School Application portal. Program Requirements for Admission: Students must have a master’s degree in a biological science or a closely related field, or a bachelor’s degree in a biological science or a closely related field with a minimum of 24 semester credit hours in biological sciences, 6 semester credit hours of calculus or statistics, and 8 semester credit hours of chemistry. An applicant with a master’s degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.5 on all previous graduate work. An applicant with a bachelor’s degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Submission of Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. Successful applicants generally have scores above the 50th percentile on all three sections (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing). A statement of purpose outlining academic background, research interests, and career goals. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or research abilities. A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. Evidence of research experience (e.g., publications, presentations, research projects). International applicants must also meet the English Language Proficiency requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program requires that the applicant possess either a master’s degree in biology or a closely related field, or a bachelor’s degree in biology or a closely related field and meet the requirements set forth by The Graduate School for unconditional admission. Applicants for the doctoral degree program will be evaluated on the basis of a thorough assessment of their academic background, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, curriculum vitae/resume, and research interests. While a master’s degree is desirable, it is not required for admission into the Ph.D. program. Specific requirements include: Graduate School application and application fee. Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores. While there is no minimum GRE score for admission, successful applicants typically score above the 50th percentile in the verbal and quantitative portions of the examination. The Analytical Writing portion of the GRE is also considered. International applicants: Official TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for international applicants unless exemption criteria are met. See The Graduate School website for current exemption criteria. Statement of Purpose: This document should indicate your area of interest in biology and identify at least three faculty members whose research expertise aligns with your interests. Curriculum Vitae or Resume. Three letters of recommendation commenting on the applicant’s academic and/or research abilities.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology with a concentration in Exercise Physiology

Requirements: Admission to the Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate degree in biomedical engineering or a related field (e.g., mechanical engineering, materials science, electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry or health sciences), a GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework and a 3.5 GPA in any graduate coursework, and strong GRE scores. Qualified applicants with a master’s degree from an ABET-accredited program may be admitted without the GRE requirement. To be considered for admission to the Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. program, prospective students must have: A baccalaureate degree in biomedical engineering or a related engineering/science/math field from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework. Strong applicants will generally have a GPA of 3.5 or higher. A graduate GPA of at least 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for any graduate coursework. Official GRE scores (verbal and quantitative sections) generally above 150. A TOEFL score of at least 79 (internet-based), or an IELTS score of at least 6.5, if English is not your native language. All applicants are required to submit a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biomedical Engineering

Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. in Business Administration requires a master’s degree in business or related field from an accredited university. Applicants with undergraduate degrees in business will be considered, but may require additional coursework. All applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Resume/Curriculum Vitae, Statement of Purpose/Letter of Intent, GRE or GMAT scores, Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Business

Requirements: In addition to the general admission requirements of The Graduate School, applicants for the PhD program in Chemistry must meet the following requirements: A statement of purpose of approximately 1-2 pages describing the applicant's prior research experience, educational and professional goals and specific research interests. Three letters of recommendation. Applicants are encouraged to submit official GRE General Test scores, but they are not required for admission. A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemistry

Requirements: All applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. The Clinical Psychology Ph.D. program requires additional materials beyond those required by the Toulouse Graduate School. Specific materials include: A personal statement that describes your interests in clinical psychology, professional goals, research experience, clinical experience, and why UNT’s program is a good fit. Three letters of recommendation (at least two from faculty who can speak to your academic and research abilities). Vita/résumé that details your academic background, research experience (e.g., publications, presentations, ongoing projects), clinical experience (e.g., practicum, volunteer work), and relevant work/volunteer history. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Official GRE general test scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing) are optional for applications for Fall 2024 and beyond. We do not accept GRE subject test scores. Minimum requirements: A bachelor’s degree in psychology or related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Completed coursework in introductory statistics and research methods with a grade of B or better. Substantial research experience (e.g., research assistant, independent study, honors thesis). Some clinical or volunteer experience is preferred.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Psychology

Requirements: Admission to UNT’s Toulouse Graduate School is a competitive process. Applicants must meet the admission requirements of both the Toulouse Graduate School and the specific degree program they are applying to. Applicants must also satisfy general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School, including official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, and English language proficiency requirements. Additional department requirements include: A UNT Graduate School Application; Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant’s academic and/or professional capabilities; A statement of purpose of not more than one page indicating the applicant’s interest in the program, research experience, and career goals; A resume or CV summarizing the applicant’s academic achievements, work experience, research publications, awards, and any other relevant experience; GRE scores are required for all applicants. The GRE must be taken within five years of the application date. Minimum scores: Verbal: 146; Quantitative: 155; Analytical Writing: 3.5; A master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field and exceptional qualifications may be admitted directly to the Ph.D. program. In this case, additional coursework may be required; A minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on all graduate work (for applicants with a master’s degree); A minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work (for applicants with a bachelor’s degree); Demonstrated research potential is highly valued. This can be evidenced by previous research projects, publications, or relevant work experience.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Computer Science and Engineering

Requirements: Application to the PhD program in Counseling Psychology will include: GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing portions of the Graduate Record Examination must be submitted. While there is no minimum required score, competitive applicants will typically score at or above the 50th percentile on the Verbal and Quantitative sections); Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; A curriculum vitae (CV); A personal statement that addresses your professional goals, experiences relevant to counseling psychology, and how the UNT Counseling Psychology program will help you achieve your goals (limit your statement to 5 double-spaced pages); A writing sample (scholarly writing, e.g., master’s thesis, research paper, publication) that demonstrates your ability to review and synthesize literature, develop a research question, and critically analyze a topic in counseling psychology; Completed graduate application (UNT online application). Preference will be given to applicants who have completed a master's degree in counseling or a closely related field (e.g., marriage and family therapy, social work, school psychology). Applicants with a master's degree in psychology or a related field (e.g., educational psychology, human development, developmental psychology) who have not completed graduate-level clinical coursework or supervised practicum experience may be required to complete additional coursework prior to full admission to the PhD program.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counseling Psychology

Requirements: Applicants to the Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision program must meet all University of North Texas and College of Education requirements for admission to graduate school, including: 1. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE): The GRE is required for admission to this program. We require a minimum combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 and a minimum Analytical Writing score of 4.0. The GRE must have been taken within the last five years. 2. Transcripts: Official transcripts of all previous college work must be submitted. 3. Resume/Vita: A current resume/vita is required. 4. Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose outlining the applicant's professional goals, research interests, and reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision at UNT is required. 5. Three Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic abilities, professional experience, and potential for success in a doctoral program are required. 6. Writing Sample: A writing sample, such as a scholarly paper or a thesis/dissertation excerpt, is required. 7. Interview: An interview with members of the Counseling and Higher Education faculty may be required.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counselor Education and Supervision

Requirements: Minimum 3.5 GPA on all graduate work prior to admission. GRE is NOT required. A current resume or curriculum vitae. A letter of intent that describes your purpose for pursuing doctoral study and your research interests (two to three pages). Evidence of scholarly writing ability such as a master’s thesis, research paper, or publication. If you do not have a writing sample of this type, you may complete a writing assessment set by the program faculty. Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of your academic ability and potential for doctoral work. Letters should be submitted to the Toulouse Graduate School directly from the recommender. Complete the Toulouse Graduate School application. Official transcripts from all institutions attended. International applicants: please see requirements at the Toulouse Graduate School.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Curriculum and Instruction
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Leadership

Requirements: Admission to the Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Psychology program is competitive and based on review of all application materials. Requirements include: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Minimum 3.5 GPA on all graduate work. A master’s degree in educational psychology or a related field (e.g., applied behavior analysis, school psychology, special education, child development, psychology, educational research) from an accredited institution. Applicants must possess coursework (e.g., minimum 18 hours or equivalent) that includes advanced statistics, research methods, and content relevant to educational psychology. Prior coursework and/or experience in these areas is considered during the review process. Please refer to the department’s website for additional information regarding specific prerequisites. Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores taken within five years of the application date. Competitive applicants will typically have scores at or above the 50th percentile on the Verbal and Quantitative sections. Scores on the Analytical Writing section are also reviewed. Three letters of recommendation from faculty or supervisors who can attest to the applicant's academic potential and professional experiences. Letters from employers are acceptable if they discuss skills and knowledge relevant to doctoral-level work in educational psychology. Statement of Purpose, which addresses how the applicant’s academic and professional goals align with the program’s mission, faculty research interests, and program offerings. Applicants should also discuss how their prior experiences have prepared them for doctoral study. Curriculum Vita (CV)/Resume. A writing sample, such as an academic paper, professional report, thesis, or dissertation chapter. The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to conduct scholarly writing and communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology

Requirements: Complete the online application to The Graduate School and pay the application fee. Official transcripts from ALL colleges and universities previously attended. Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. A minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours attempted. A statement of purpose outlining career goals, research interests, how this program aligns with those interests, and how the applicant’s background and experience have prepared them for doctoral study. A current resume or curriculum vitae outlining academic, research, and work experience. An academic writing sample (e.g., a published article, research report, or term paper). Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant’s academic and/or research potential. An interview (typically virtual) with program faculty may be required.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology with a concentration in Learning Sciences

Requirements:
Required application materials for this program include:
*   Three letters of recommendation
*   Official transcripts
*   Statement of Purpose
*   Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
*   GRE Scores are OPTIONAL for Fall 2024, Spring 2025, and Fall 2025 admissions. The program code is 6480.
*   International applicants whose native language is not English must submit proof of English proficiency.
  *   Acceptable scores on standardized tests such as the TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE are required.
  *   For specific score requirements, please refer to the UNT International website.
  *   UNT does not accept the Duolingo English Test.
  *   This requirement can be waived under certain conditions as outlined on the UNT International website.

International applicants also need to review the additional requirements for admission listed on the UNT International website.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering

Requirements: To be admitted to the Ph.D. program, prospective students must: Satisfy the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. Have a M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with a minimum GPA of 3.5. Complete the Electrical Engineering Ph.D. Application. A minimum GRE revised General Test score of 153 on the verbal portion, 153 on the quantitative portion, and 4.0 on the analytical writing portion. The GRE requirement may be waived if the applicant holds a master’s degree from an accredited U.S. university with a GPA of 3.5 or higher. Three letters of recommendation. A Statement of Purpose outlining the applicant’s interest in the program and research goals. A Resume or Curriculum Vitae. For international students, a TOEFL or IELTS score is required. Refer to the International Graduate Student Admissions page for details.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering with a concentration in Biomedical Engineering

Requirements:
For Admission to the Program:
Admission to the PhD program in English is highly selective and is made by the graduate faculty in English. The department admits students who have demonstrated scholarly excellence and who are prepared to undertake advanced research in a specialized field.
Minimum requirements for admission include:
1. A master’s degree in English or a related field from an accredited university. Applicants with a master’s degree in a related field, or with only a bachelor’s degree, may be required to take additional courses.
2. A minimum 3.5 grade point average (GPA) in graduate coursework.
3. Materials to be submitted as part of the application for admission to the PhD program in English are:
   1. Official transcripts of all previous college work.
   2. Statement of Purpose (no more than 750 words).
   3. Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume.
   4. Writing Sample (15–20 pages).
   5. Three letters of recommendation.
   6. International applicants must also submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores (see “International Admission”).
The Graduate School requires international applicants to demonstrate English language proficiency through one of several options. See the International Admission section of the Graduate Catalog for details.
Application Deadlines
Fall: January 15
Spring: October 15
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in English

Requirements: An earned master’s degree in an environmental science-related field or a bachelor's degree in a closely related science, engineering or social science field. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all previous graduate work. GRE (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) scores are required. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing the applicant's research interests and career goals. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic and research abilities. A current curriculum vitae or résumé. International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and provide the materials specified below for their application file to be considered complete. Required application materials include: CV or resume, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing), Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International applicants must also provide a TOEFL or IELTS score. A score of 79 on the TOEFL iBT or 6.5 on the IELTS is required. Please visit the Graduate School Admissions page for more information.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Ecology and Conservation Biology

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Environmental Science Ph.D. program, you must first apply to the Toulouse Graduate School. The Toulouse Graduate School requires a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Official transcripts of all previous college work must be submitted. Specific admission requirements for the Environmental Science Ph.D. program include: Completion of a master's degree in environmental science, a natural science, or a related field, or a bachelor's degree in one of those areas with significant relevant work experience. Minimum combined verbal and quantitative GRE scores of 300 (new score scale) or 1000 (old score scale). Scores must be less than five years old. (See GRE waiver criteria below) A current resume or curriculum vitae. A Statement of Purpose explaining your background, interests, and professional goals related to environmental science. Three letters of recommendation. International students must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Geoscience

Requirements: Admission to the Environmental Science Ph.D. program requires applicants to have an M.S. degree, or its equivalent, in environmental science or a related discipline. Exceptionally qualified applicants may be admitted to the Ph.D. program directly from a B.S. or B.A. degree. The GRE revised General Test is required for all applicants. A GRE score of 150 on the verbal and 150 on the quantitative reasoning sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing section is expected. Applicants for the PhD in Environmental Science program must have an overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all undergraduate and graduate work OR a 3.5 GPA on all graduate work.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Human Ecology

Requirements: Minimum Requirements for Admission: Baccalaureate or master's degree from an accredited institution. A master's degree is highly encouraged but not strictly required. Students entering with a bachelor's degree must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) on all work attempted while those entering with a master's degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.5 (on a 4.0 scale) on all work attempted at the master's level. GRE verbal and quantitative scores are required for all PhD applicants. There is no minimum score required, but competitive applicants typically score above the 50th percentile on both sections. Scores must be less than five years old at the time of application. The GRE requirement may be waived for exceptional master’s students already enrolled in our department’s program. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. All applicants must submit the following documents to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all institutions attended, GRE scores, Letter of intent / Statement of Purpose: (1-2 pages in length) indicating your qualifications for pursuing a Ph.D. in Environmental Science, your research interests and experience, and your career goals. Include the names of faculty members with whom you would like to work. Note: This is an important part of your application. Make sure to clearly state your research interests and identify faculty members you are interested in working with. CV / Resume: A list of educational, professional and research experiences, publications, presentations, awards, and other relevant information. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability, research experience, and/or professional experience. International applicants must submit a copy of their academic evaluation, financial statement and other documents specific to international student applications.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Science Education Research

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program is based on the recommendation of the Environmental Science Program faculty. All applicants must meet the general admission requirements for graduate studies outlined in the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog. In addition, applicants must meet the following program requirements: A master’s degree in environmental science or a related discipline from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree may be admitted directly to the PhD program under exceptional circumstances. A GPA of at least 3.0 on all work leading to the master’s degree and on any work attempted beyond the master’s degree. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree seeking direct admission to the PhD program must have a GPA of at least 3.5 on all undergraduate work. Submission of GRE scores (general test). International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. See the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog for accepted methods of demonstrating English language proficiency. Applicants are encouraged to contact specific faculty members regarding research interests. All doctoral programs also require a CV or resume, a statement of purpose, and most doctoral programs require at least three letters of recommendation. Other general graduate admissions requirements include an application for admission, application fee, and official transcripts.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Toxicology

Requirements:
Admission to the doctoral program requires an undergraduate degree and a master’s degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts of all college-level work must be submitted to the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition, the applicant must meet the following minimum requirements:
* A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on all undergraduate work or a 3.5 on all graduate work.
* A minimum combined score of 300 on the verbal and quantitative portions of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) and a minimum score of 3.5 on the analytical writing portion. The GRE must have been taken within five years of the date of application.
* Three letters of recommendation submitted directly from the person providing the recommendation.
* Statement of purpose (one page) indicating the applicant’s interest in the program, career goals and experience relevant to the program.
* Resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Health Sciences

*   Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
*   Have a minimum 2.8 undergraduate GPA on a 4.0 scale or 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
*   Have completed an introductory programming course in Python or R with a grade of B or higher.
*   Have completed an introductory statistics course with a grade of B or higher.
*   Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   International applicants must meet additional requirements.
Program name: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Analytics

Requirements:
Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Engineering program is competitive. Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and additional program requirements listed below.
Program Admission Requirements:
*   Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
*   Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 undergraduate hours.
*   Background in computer science, information science, mathematics, statistics, or a closely related field. Applicants with backgrounds in other fields may be admitted on a conditional basis and may be required to complete specific prerequisite courses.
*   Personal Statement: A statement of purpose outlining career goals and reasons for pursuing the certificate.
*   Résumé/CV: Highlighting academic background, relevant work experience, and any research or projects.
*   Letters of Recommendation (optional): Applicants may submit up to three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with their academic or professional qualifications.
*   Applicants are encouraged to submit GRE scores, though they are not required.
Program name: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Engineering

Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science is a two-step process. First, students must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School. Second, they must apply directly to the Department of Computer Science and Engineering for program acceptance. Departmental Admission Requirements: In addition to the requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, students seeking the Data Science Graduate Academic Certificate must meet the following departmental requirements: 1. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with an adequate undergraduate GPA (generally, a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale in the last 60 undergraduate hours and any graduate work). 2. Undergraduate preparation for the certificate program is satisfied by earning a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, data science, information science, mathematics, statistics or a related field. 3. Students who have not earned a bachelor's degree in a related field may be admitted to the certificate program provisionally upon recommendation of the department. These students will be required to demonstrate competency through examinations, coursework or other evidence in the following areas: calculus, linear algebra, basic probability and statistics, data structures, and object-oriented programming. 4. Students must submit the following directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all universities attended. GRE is not required for this certificate. A statement of purpose outlining academic interests, relevant experience and career goals. A current resume or CV. Two letters of recommendation (optional but recommended).
Program name: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science

Program name: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School and specific requirements for the certificate. For admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Applicants who do not meet the minimum GPA may be admitted to the certificate program on probation by the department. Applicants for the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management must meet the specific requirements for admission to the master’s program in the Department of Information Science or have a graduate degree in a related field and be in good academic standing. Students should apply via the Graduate School online application or complete the 'Add a Graduate Academic Certificate' form.
Program name: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management
